text:
CHRIST JESUS—THE ULTIMATE REDEEMER

📖In whom we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of sins, according to the riches of his grace (Ephesians 1:7).

Redemption is one of the beautiful truths in the Gospel because it reveals not only what Christ accomplished, but also who He is. The Scriptures present the picture of a redeemer as one who has both the legal right and the ability to secure another's freedom. In the Lord Jesus Christ, we find the perfect and ultimate fulfilment ofthat picture. He is the Redeemer who paid the full price for our salvation and brought us into everlasting freedom. 

In the law of Moses, a kinsman-redeemer could redeem a relative who had fallen into debt or bondage. The redeemer had a legal right to act on behalf of the one in need, but he also had to pay the required price. Freedom wasn't obtained by mere desire or good intentions; a price had to be paid. 

This helps us understandthe significance of Christ'ssacrifice.Humanity'sgreatest problem was notmerely the devil's oppression; it was the issue of sin. Sin had brought separation from God and placed mankind under judgment. The righteousdemandsofjusticehad to be satisfied.A price had to be paid. 

What a blessing to know that the Lord Jesus took our place and paid the full price required for our redemption. The payment wasn't silver or gold; it was His precious blood. The Bible says, *“Forasmuch as ye know that ye were not redeemed with corruptible things, as silver and gold…But with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot”* (1 Peter 1:18-19). 

When He shed His blood, He obtained eternal redemption for us. The debt was settled. The claims against us were satisfied.The penaltyofsinwasfullyaddressed. The Lord Jesus paid the price you could never pay. He accomplished what you could never accomplish for yourself. 

Through His sacrifice, you've been brought into righteousness and fellowship with God. He met every demand of divine justice, paid the full price with His own blood, and secured your eternal liberty. Therefore, live with gratitude and confidence, knowing that your salvation is eternally secure in Him.

       *🙏PRAYER*
Dear Father, I thank you for the redemption that is mine through the blood of Jesus Christ. I rejoice in the knowledge that the full price for my salvation has been paid. I walk in righteousness, in fellowship with you, and in grateful acknowledgment of the fulfilment of the full blessings of the Gospel in my life, in Jesus' Name. Amen.

*FURTHER STUDY📖=>*
 *1 Peter 1:18-19 NIV*
For you know that it was not with perishable things such as silver or gold that you were redeemed from the empty way of life handed down to you from your ancestors, [19] but with the precious blood of Christ, a lamb without blemish or defect.

*Hebrews 9:11-15 KJV*
 But Christ being come an high priest of good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this building; [12] Neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us. [13] For if the blood of bulls and of goats, and the ashes of an heifer sprinkling the unclean, sanctifieth to the purifying of the flesh: [14] How much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to God, purge your conscience from dead works to serve the living God? [15] And for this cause he is the mediator of the new testament, that by means of death, for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first testament, they which are called might receive the promise of eternal inheritance.

*📖DAILY SCRIPTURE READING📖*

author: rupertpitt1

text:
The Long March Through France's Institutions Has Reached the Streets

France's burning town halls and barricaded schools did not emerge from nowhere. Grievances over teacher shortages, neglected buildings and public spending were real. So was the willingness of revolutionary activists to exploit them. Behind the disorder lies a question European governments have avoided for decades: what happens when institutions become battlegrounds for competing ideologies while foreign powers exploit the divisions?

In the late 1960s, the revolutionary Left embraced the long march through the institutions. Universities, education, journalism and public administration offered opportunities to reshape society over generations. France already possessed a formidable communist tradition, but 1968 gave institutional radicalism new momentum. Fifty years later, the language remains familiar. Capitalism is oppression, Western power is imperialism, and established authority exists to be challenged.

Alongside this developed another movement with different ambitions. The Muslim Brotherhood pursued influence through religious associations, education, charities and community representation. France's Interior Ministry warned in 2025 about its institutional strategy. Its report identified Étudiants musulmans de France as associated with Brotherhood-linked organisations. In February's student welfare elections, EMF-backed lists gained eleven representatives. On 15 October, EMF publicly supported the school demonstrations.

The revolutionary Left and political Islam envisage profoundly different societies. One draws upon Marxism, the other religious authority. Yet Gaza has demonstrated how readily their campaigns converge. Communist student organisations, Islamist-associated networks and pro-Palestinian movements can advance the same immediate cause despite disagreements about what follows. The Iranian Revolution offers a warning. Secular leftists helped overthrow the Shah alongside Islamists, only to discover that Khomeini's victorious movement had little tolerance for former allies.

Then there is the money. Investigative reporting has documented Qatar's historical financing of religious and cultural institutions in Europe. A French judicial investigation has examined alleged Qatari payments to political and media intermediaries. Le Monde reported evidence pointing towards Qatari entities in an influence operation involving French contacts. None establishes Qatari involvement in the riots, but the findings raise questions about foreign money purchasing influence inside democratic societies.

China, Russia and Iran present further concerns. Reporting has linked a Shanghai-based financier accused of promoting Beijing's interests to international activist media networks. French intelligence has documented Russian disinformation operations. Iran maintains intelligence and proxy networks across Europe. On 13 October, France's foreign minister warned that foreign actors were exploiting divisions over immigration, secularism and Israel-Palestine. Their role in the violence remains unproven, but their interest in exploiting it is clear.

The danger lies in examining everything separately. University radicalism becomes education policy. Islamist influence falls to religious regulators. Foreign financing goes to investigators. Disinformation becomes an intelligence matter. Meanwhile, the political consequences accumulate across institutions entrusted with preserving a common civic culture.

France must establish who organised the violence, who financed the surrounding networks and whether foreign interests played any operational role. But the deeper questions will remain when the streets are cleared. Decades of ideological influence cannot be undone by arresting rioters.

A republic cannot preserve its authority indefinitely while refusing to examine who shapes the loyalties, assumptions and ambitions of the generations it educates.

text:
Bitcoin Movies and Documentaries

Media Man Crypto Watercooler

Money Electric: The Bitcoin Mystery (2024, HBO) Directed by Cullen Hoback, this documentary investigates Bitcoin’s origins and the identity of its creator, Satoshi Nakamoto. It offers a thrilling, globe-spanning narrative with new clues about Bitcoin’s rise. Available on HBO and Max.

Banking on Bitcoin (2016, Netflix) A popular documentary exploring Bitcoin’s roots, its potential to disrupt traditional banking, and its early challenges. Features interviews with key figures like Erik Voorhees and Charlie Shrem. Available on Netflix and other platforms.

The Rise and Rise of Bitcoin (2014) Follows programmer Daniel Mross, an early Bitcoin enthusiast, documenting Bitcoin’s volatile journey and its community. Ideal for beginners, it avoids technical jargon and includes figures like Brian Armstrong. Available on Prime Video, iTunes, and Fandango at Home.

Bitcoin: The End of Money as We Know It (2015) A concise 60-minute crash course on money’s evolution and Bitcoin’s role as a decentralized alternative. Features Andreas Antonopoulos and Roger Ver. Won awards at the Amsterdam Film Festival. Available on various platforms.

God Bless Bitcoin (2025, YouTube) Explores Bitcoin as a solution to broken monetary systems, featuring Bitcoin advocates and interfaith leaders. Free to watch on YouTube.

text:
Virginia Board of Psychology revokes license of psychologist Katie S. Kelly for sexual relationship with patient

The Virginia Board of Psychology has entered a consent order affecting the license of clinical psychologist Katie Sinclair Kelly after finding she engaged in a romantic and sexual relationship with a patient while continuing to provide therapy.

Kelly was first licensed on June 29, 2017. Her license was summarily suspended on February 12, 2026. The Board found that, beginning in March 2022, she violated regulations governing confidentiality, boundaries, and professional conduct by initiating and maintaining a sexual relationship with “Patient A,” a woman she treated from January 2021 to August 2023. Patient A had a reported history of childhood sexual abuse and later multiple sexual assaults, including rape.

Findings detail progressive boundary violations: personal disclosures about Kelly’s marriage and substance-use history, invitations to her home, offers of alcohol, requests for rides when intoxicated, and physical contact such as sitting on the patient’s lap. Text messages and other evidence showed the relationship became romantic and sexual after Kelly kissed the patient; sexual activity then occurred regularly, primarily at Kelly’s home, while therapy continued. Patient A reported one instance of non-consensual digital penetration of her rectum. Kelly instructed the patient to keep the relationship secret, delete messages, and refer to her as “Dr. Kelly” only during sessions. The patient’s mental health deteriorated, including worsening of an eating disorder requiring residential treatment, increased self-harm, and a suicide attempt after the relationship ended.

Additional violations committed by Kelly included practicing outside the scope of psychology by giving the patient medication advice and providing her a controlled substance; inadequate record-keeping for Patient A and other clients, and serving simultaneously as therapist and parenting coordinator in a dual role. Under investigation, Kelly denied the romantic and sexual allegations.

Source: Consent Order in re: Katie Sinclair Kelly LCP, lic. no. 0810-005728, case nos. 230850 & 234034, Virginia Board of Psychology, June 22, 2026.
